Your name is at the top. "The Ancestor is prepared to let it stop accruing, if you stop using it. Otherwise, I come back, and it does not."

choices.text: Agree to stop it accruing

effects.log: {npc} writes a very small line. You feel a weight come off you that you had not known about. It is not a nice feeling, and that was also intended.

choices.text: Knock the book out of {his} hands

ok.log: It is a very ugly fight, and {npc} does not stop writing the entire time. At the end of it {he} blots the page with {his} sleeve. "Noted," {he} says.

fail.log: You are on the ground. {He} is standing on your hand, not hard, while {he} finishes the line. "Noted," {npc} says.

choices.text: Pay it all off

effects.log: It is a very large figure, in the old reckoning. {He} rules it off, and shuts the book, and for the first time looks you in the eye, and it is not an improvement.

events.text: {npc} is sitting on your bed, with the book open. "Arrears," {he} says. "I did mention." {He} has brought a friend this time, or something that was once. It does not look as if it has been told what you have done. It has only been told your name.

choices.text: Settle it here

ok.log: The room is a ruin. {npc} tears out a page, hands it to you, and limps to the door. "A partial payment," {he} says, "has been received."

fail.log: You wake up with a new line on your page, and no idea when {he} wrote it. It has been a long night, and you are told so in a very neat hand.

choices.text: Out of the door, and do not look back

ok.log: You do not look back. You hear a page being turned behind you, quite quietly, all the way down the stairs.

fail.log: Whatever it was has got to the stairs first. You get past it, at some cost, and you do not look at what it was.

events.text: {npc} comes on the day appointed and opens your account. "They took a security against your meridians," {he} says. "It is entered here. It may be redeemed. It says redemption by force of arms is allowed, by a very old clause. I did not write it. I do hope you will not try."

choices.text: Invoke the old clause

ok.log: You redeem it. {npc} enters it through a split lip, in a hand that does not shake at all. Your meridians are yours again, and it says so on the page.

fail.log: The clause is exercised unsuccessfully. A small fee is added. {He} regrets it, and tells you the date of the next opportunity.

choices.text: Ask {him} what the interest is

effects.log: {He} tells you. It takes a while. You see {him} out.

events.text: A cord comes by post, red, and neatly tied in the old way. It means that your page has been ruled off and closed, as uncollectable. Sister Ran has written across it, in very small letters, a word you have to hold up to the lamp. It says "Sold." You decide not to ask.

events.text: Beopjin walks you as far as the first turn of the stairs, which the elder has never done for anyone you know of. "You will not teach it," the elder says. It is not a question. "Then come back for New Year, there will be plain rice." The old monk is already looking at the leaves.

choices.text: Give your word, and go

effects.log: You give it. It is a strange sort of lightness, walking down that road with everything you learned and nobody behind you. You keep your hands quite carefully to yourself.

choices.text: Ask them to teach you one last thing

effects.log: They look at you. Then they do, as it happens: something small, and of no use in a fight. You will still be thinking about it when you are old.

events.text: A novice comes three days down the road, out of breath, carrying a bag of pears and a message from the elder: nothing at all, the novice says, they just thought that you might like pears. The temple remembers its own.

choices.text: Send your thanks

effects.log: You write it out. It does not take long, and it is more than they expected. Somebody up there keeps your letter, you hear.

choices.text: Say nothing, and remember it

effects.log: You say nothing, as you were taught. It sits in you quite warmly for a good while.

events.text: The pears stop coming. A letter arrives instead, in an elder's shaking hand, and it contains only the words you swore, copied out once. Then a novice shows up at your gate, sees your disciples at their practice, bows to no one, and goes home.

choices.text: Stand by what you taught

effects.log: Your students are good. They will be very good. You have told yourself this several times now, and you keep looking up the road. They want it back, and if you use it in the open, they will come.

choices.text: Write back, and try to explain

effects.log: It is a very long letter. Nobody answers. There was never going to be an answer. What was given was the one thing they asked you not to give.

events.text: Old Yeon Cheol sees you off at the stream. "Do not teach it to anyone," he says. "It only goes wrong when it is taught anyway." He gives you a very small and unremarkable stone, for no reason, and goes back to not looking at you.

events.text: Registrar Gu has the undertaking ready, and turns it to you. You will not teach the house's arts. It is very short. "Your record stands," the registrar says, blotting it. "It goes with you. Should you ever need a reference, write. I will tell them the truth."

events.text: Your page has come off leave. You know this because of the tidy person sitting in your hall when you come in, with the book already open, looking at your disciples. They say "Teaching,", in a tone of mild interest, and turns to a fresh line.

events.text: A new novice has heard you hold the vow, and follows you round the yard for a week, asking how. You do not know how. You have started to do your morning work rather more carefully, in case it is being taken down.

choices.text: Show them the dull parts

effects.log: You show them the dull parts. They are disappointed, and they stay. So, you notice, do you.

choices.text: Tell them to go and ask the elders

effects.log: They go. You get your mornings back. It was rather nice being taken for someone who knew.

events.text: A hall elder has asked, quietly, whether your vow might bend in a small matter of the house's convenience: a word that need not be said, a thing that need not be seen. It would be a real help to everyone. You have been very well treated here.

choices.text: Keep to it, and take the cold shoulder

effects.log: You keep to it. The elder is very polite to you after that. Your rank comes no easier, and you sleep fine.

choices.text: Find a way to help that does not quite touch it

effects.log: It takes a lot of lawyering, in your own head. The elder is pleased. You are not sure what you have just learned about yourself.

events.text: The creed on the wall is yours, and so is the vow, and your disciples have noticed there is nobody to check whether you are keeping it. A bright one has asked you, in the hall, in front of the others, who holds the founder to account.

choices.text: Tell them that they do, and mean it

effects.log: Now they do. It is much more uncomfortable than you imagined, and the hall has never run better.

choices.text: Tell them the founder answers to the Way

effects.log: It is a very good answer. They write it down. The bright one looks at you for a little longer than necessary.

events.text: Another founder, older and much richer, has told you over wine that vows are for people who still have something to prove. "You have a hall," they say. "Let it keep the vow for you. That is what halls are for." It sounds like advice. They have a very nice hall.

choices.text: Thank them, and go home to your leaking roof

effects.log: You go home. It leaks. You sit under it with some satisfaction, and a bucket.

choices.text: Ask them how it works, out of interest

effects.log: They tell you, in some detail. You do not do it. You do remember every word of it, though.

events.text: In the ruins you rebuilt, you find a stone with the old masters' precept on it, half worn away. It is not quite the vow you swore. Some of it is better. A few of your people, who are very proud of the old house, have seen you looking at it.

choices.text: Set it in the wall beside your own

effects.log: It is an odd pair. People will argue about it for years, and that is a good thing for a house to have.

choices.text: Have it carried to the store-room, gently

effects.log: It is very gently done. The old-house people do not say anything, and they do not forget it.

events.text: Somebody has come who remembers what the old sect did to their family, before it fell. You did not do it. You rebuilt it, and you took the name, and you swore on what it stood for. They stand very straight in your courtyard and ask you what you mean to do about that.

choices.text: Pay what the old house owes

effects.log: You pay, in silver and in words. It is a long afternoon. It is the first time that anyone has really treated you as the head of that house.

choices.text: Tell them the old house is gone

effects.log: They look round at your walls, slowly. Then they go, and you do not feel you have won anything.

events.text: Going through your predecessor's things, you find they kept the vow much worse than anyone said, and that they wrote down each time, and how sorry they were. There are a great many pages. It is an extremely human document. It is also very useful to anyone who wanted to hurt the house.

choices.text: Keep the pages, and read one every year

effects.log: You do. It keeps you honest in ways no elder could. You cannot quite say that you have forgiven them, but you know them now.

choices.text: Burn them

effects.log: It is done in a small brazier. You know them just as well as you did, now, and nobody else ever will.

events.text: The old elders tell you how it was done in your predecessor's day, as they do. Very often. Today it is how the vow was kept, which is apparently not how you keep it. The elders have been right about a lot of things, it must be said, and you have had a hard week.

choices.text: Hear them out, and then do it your way

effects.log: You hear them to the end, and then you do what you were going to do. They grumble, and they follow. It is what they are for.

choices.text: Do it their way, this time

effects.log: It works fine. It works very well. They look at you with fond approval, and it feels a little like being patted.

events.text: At the clan table an uncle of the house has asked why a child of this house needs an outside vow on top of the family rule. It is a fair question. The oldest woman at the table has stopped eating so as to hear the answer. So have the cousins, who will be repeating it.

choices.text: Tell them what it has cost you, and what it has given

effects.log: It is a very quiet table, for a moment. The old woman goes back to her soup, and passes you the good pickles.

choices.text: Say it does not conflict, and change the subject

effects.log: It does not, mostly. The pickles do not come your way, and the cousins go on looking at you.

events.text: A cousin has done something shameful, and the house wants it hidden. They have all assumed that you will help, as blood does. It runs very close to what you swore. The house has fed you all your life.

choices.text: Help in every way that does not touch the vow

effects.log: You do what you can within it, and you say plainly where it stops. It is noticed. You are now a difficult relation.

choices.text: Stand aside, and let the house do it

effects.log: You see nothing, for a week, on purpose. Your vow is intact. So is the family's opinion of you. It is a very narrow place to stand.

events.text: The house looks to you, and now the whole family has started to keep your vow on your behalf, badly. A nephew has challenged someone for mentioning it. An aunt of the house has given up meat, and is angry with you about it. You did not ask for any of this.

choices.text: Tell them all that the vow is yours, not theirs

effects.log: They are hurt, and then relieved. The aunt has a large dinner. You are left alone with it, and you find you like that better.

choices.text: Let them; it is good for a house to believe in something

effects.log: It is, very likely. By the end of the year your name on a vow is doing things you never meant.

events.text: A branch line sends word that they will back you in the coming family meeting, if you will let one small clause of your vow lapse in a matter touching their trade. It is the first decent offer they have ever made. You can count the votes as well as they can.

choices.text: Refuse, and count the votes again

effects.log: It is close, and you come through it, not by much. The branch sends a very stiff note, and you frame it.

choices.text: Find something else they might want

effects.log: It costs you a good deal more silver than you had planned. They take it. They had only wanted to see if you would blink.

events.text: It has come up in the ancestral hall: should every head of this house hold the vow you hold, from now on? The elders are for it. You think of your heir, and what you would be binding them to, and what they might one day be tempted to do about it.

choices.text: Leave it to each head to choose

effects.log: It goes down in the book that it was offered, and declined. Your heir will never know how close it came, and you are glad.

choices.text: Make it the rule of the house

effects.log: It is carved up the same day. It looks magnificent. A hundred years is a long time, and you try not to think about that.

events.text: The family's oldest tablet has a line of your ancestor's on it that nobody has read aloud for two generations. You have had it read to you. It is rather like your vow, and rather less forgiving. Nobody knows you asked. The hall is empty, and the incense has gone out.

choices.text: Light it again, and stay a while

effects.log: You stay a while. It is not as if anybody answers. You leave feeling that you have been looked at by someone with a very long memory.

choices.text: Have the line copied, and hung where the heir will see it

effects.log: It is done before breakfast. Your heir walks past it every day, and has not said anything yet.

events.text: A minister has pointed out, with great respect, that a ruler who has sworn a private vow has a second master. The Mandate does not like a second master. He is a good minister. He would like to know which of them is to come first, in writing, before the budget.

choices.text: Write that the vow holds you to the realm, and sign it

effects.log: He reads it several times. It is good law, and he is rather moved, though he conceals it. The budget goes through.

choices.text: Tell him the throne has no need to answer that

effects.log: It does not. He bows, very low. You see him making a note as he goes out backward.

events.text: The court has found a very fine old precedent by which a ruler's vow may be kept by a proxy, for a fee, in a temple somewhere. Half your predecessors did it, it seems. The temple has already sent a brochure, on silk. You would not have to do anything at all, ever again.

choices.text: Send back the silk, and keep it yourself

effects.log: Your court finds this deeply eccentric. By the end of the year several ministers are quietly reading up on what they ought to be doing as well.

choices.text: Keep the silk, and think about it

effects.log: It is lovely silk. You think about it. It is in a drawer, within reach.

events.text: A hall master has asked you, in the way they do, whether your oath means you are getting ideas. Everyone who has ever got ideas in the Mountains has had that very conversation, on these very stairs. The hall master seems entirely at ease. The stairs are steep.

choices.text: Say it means you are the most reliable person here

effects.log: It is a good answer, and even true. They laugh, and pat your shoulder, and you go on down the stairs with care.

choices.text: Ask them how long they have held their own

effects.log: Their face does not change at all. It is the most interesting thing that has happened on those stairs this year.

events.text: There is a new one in your charge, younger than they look, who has taken your oath for a sort of religion. They bring you things. They watch you. They have started to do small cruel things for you, without being asked, on the theory that you would like it.

choices.text: Teach them what it is actually for

effects.log: You tell them, once, in a very few words. They do not bring you anything after that. They are the better for it, and so is the stair.

choices.text: Let them; it is useful

effects.log: It is useful. You could not say, these days, exactly who is keeping the oath on whom.

events.text: Your page has been looking better, and Sister Ran mentions it, as a doctor might mention a mole. People have started to ask you for small loans against the Ancestor's favour. You had not known that that could be done. It seems that it is done all the time.

choices.text: Lend nothing, and keep your page clean

effects.log: You lend nothing. It makes you very unpopular on the lower floors. Ran nods, and turns the page.

choices.text: Lend a little, and enter it

effects.log: You enter it. It makes you a good many friends, of the kind you have here. Your page is getting complicated.

events.text: They are saying in the deep hall that the Ancestor is pleased with you. You go down to find out who is saying it. The hall is empty and nothing is said at all. On your way back up, you notice that you were walking very carefully, as if not to wake anyone.

choices.text: Do not go down there again without being called

effects.log: You stay upstairs. Nothing happens. You have started to think that is the most worrying part.

choices.text: Go down every year, and sit

effects.log: You sit there. There is no one there. At some point in the fifth year you begin to find it restful, and that also goes on your page.

events.text: A delegate from the south has asked if your personal vow means you will favour your own in the Alliance's business. It is a reasonable question, asked by someone who would very much like you to say something foolish. The minutes are being taken by a very bored young person.

choices.text: Answer it on the record, in plain words

effects.log: It goes in the minutes. The bored young person looks up for the first time this year. It will be quoted at you for a generation, mostly with approval.

choices.text: Refer it to committee

effects.log: It goes to committee. That is where it lives now, for the rest of your career, along with the question of who sits where.

events.text: A hard case: the Alliance has voted, properly, to do something which your vow says you should not. You could recuse yourself, and it will happen anyway, with your hands clean. Everyone agrees that this is the honourable thing to do. It is, you notice, also extremely convenient.

choices.text: Vote against, and stay in the room

effects.log: You lose nineteen to one, and you have to carry the order out yourself, in your own way. It is the hardest year of your service, and you would do it again.

choices.text: Recuse yourself

effects.log: Your hands are very clean. You look at them a good deal, over the next while.
